acceptance_criteria.criterion: GET /api/projects returns paginated envelope { projects, total, page, limit, total_pages, status_counts }
Default request returns page 1, limit 50, status ACTIVE (no archived)
?page=2&limit=25 returns the correct second page of 25 items
?search=foo filters by substring match on slug, project_name, repository_name
Out-of-range page returns empty projects with correct metadata

summary: Implemented server-side pagination for GET /api/projects (WP-007).

gui/api.ts: Added ProjectListParams, ProjectListEnvelope, ProjectSortField interfaces. Refactored handleListProjects to accept rawParams and return a paginated envelope { projects, total, page, limit, total_pages, status_counts }.
Processing pipeline: enrich all projects → apply search filter → compute status_counts (from search-filtered set before status filter) → apply status filter → sort → paginate.

Param validation: page clamped >=1; limit clamped [1,200] with correct 0-value handling; status validated against known values (default ACTIVE); sort validated against supported fields (default last_updated); dir defaults to desc.
gui/server.ts: Updated GET /api/projects route to parse URLSearchParams from the request URL and pass params to handleListProjects.

tests/gui/api.test.ts: Updated all existing handleListProjects usages from array-return to envelope-return (results.projects.find / results.projects.map). Added 22 new WP-007 tests covering envelope shape, pagination, status filtering, search filtering, sorting, and status_counts. All 1200 tests pass.

comments.note: handleListProjects now enriches ALL projects in memory before paginating. With the WP-006 cache this is fast (just .meta.json reads), but if cache is cold for many projects the first load could be slow. A future optimisation could lazy-enrich only the page slice (acceptable tradeoff for now).

summary: All 10 ACs verified. GET /api/projects returns a correct paginated envelope. All 22 new tests pass (1200/1200 total).
Param validation verified: page clamped >=1; limit clamped [1,200] with 0-value handled as 1; invalid status defaults to ACTIVE; invalid sort defaults to last_updated; dir defaults to desc.
Processing pipeline is correct: enrich all → search filter → status_counts (pre-status-filter) → status filter → sort → paginate.
ACTIVE status filter correctly excludes only ARCHIVED projects. ALL includes everything. Specific status values filter exactly.
search filter applies case-insensitive substring match to slug, project_name, and repository_name.
Out-of-range page returns empty pageSlice with correct total and total_pages metadata.

KNOWN IMPACT: Frontend currently broken because app.js treats the response as a plain array. WP-008 is required to unwrap the envelope and render pagination controls before end-to-end testing is possible.

comments.note: BREAKING FRONTEND CHANGE (by design, pending WP-008): GET /api/projects now returns { projects, total, page, limit, total_pages, status_counts } instead of a plain array. app.js calls API.getProjects().then(projects => render(projects)) where render()/buildTable() calls projects.length and sortProjects().slice() — both operations will fail on the envelope object, breaking the project list view. This is the intentional pre-condition for WP-008. WP-008 must be implemented before the feature can be tested end-to-end.
status_counts computation uses the search-filtered set before the status filter is applied. This matches the spec intent and supports filter badge counts. Correct.

limit=0 edge case: Math.floor(0)=0, then Math.max(1, 0)=1, so limit=0 is clamped to 1. This is correct per the spec ('limit clamped [1,200] with correct 0-value handling') but not explicitly documented in the inline comments. Low risk.
total_pages = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total / limit)) — correctly returns 1 when total=0 (empty list). Correct.

summary: Code review PASS for gui/api.ts (handleListProjects refactor) and gui/server.ts (route update) for WP-007.

Architecture: 6-step pipeline (enrich → search filter → status_counts → status filter → sort → paginate) is clearly documented in JSDoc and implemented in sequential order. Easy to follow and maintain.

ProjectListParams uses number | string union to accommodate raw query string values, avoiding a parsing layer. Sanitization handles all edge cases: limit=0 → 1, NaN → defaults, out-of-range page → 1, invalid sort/status → defaults. total_pages = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/limit)) correctly returns 1 for empty lists.

Parameter validation uses Set<> whitelist lookups for both status filter (VALID_STATUS_FILTERS) and sort field (SORT_FIELDS). No user-controlled input reaches file I/O directly. Search uses string includes(), no regex injection risk.
server.ts route uses URLSearchParams to parse the query string; sp.get(key) ?? undefined maps absent params to undefined cleanly, matching optional typed interface.

22 new tests in 5 describe blocks cover all ACs: envelope shape, pagination arithmetic, status filtering (ALL/ACTIVE/specific), search substring matching, sorting, and status_counts pre-filter semantics. Existing tests updated to unwrap .projects from the envelope. All 1200 tests pass.
The ACTIVE filter (default) correctly excludes only ARCHIVED projects; CANCELLED is included in ACTIVE — consistent with VALID_STATUS_FILTERS including CANCELLED as a queryable status.
Known pre-condition for WP-008: frontend app.js currently broken because it expects a plain array. This is intentional and tracked.
All 10 ACs are met.

comments.note: gui/api.ts handleListProjects: SORT_FIELDS and VALID_STATUS_FILTERS are Set<> instances providing O(1) lookup for param validation. Clean and correct.

gui/api.ts sort case 'done': sorts by (total_work_packages - pending_work_packages) — absolute completed count, not percentage. The frontend sorts by percentage. For projects with different total WP counts the orderings diverge. This is a reasonable tradeoff (server can't sort by percentage without extra calculation) and the difference is minor. Low priority.
gui/server.ts: sp.get(key) ?? undefined correctly maps absent params to undefined, matching ProjectListParams optionality. No extra null-to-undefined unwrapping needed elsewhere.

status_counts computed from search-filtered set before status filter: correct semantic for filter badge counts. The specific test 'status_counts are computed from search-filtered set (before status filter)' explicitly validates this design decision.
